title: A bench that can change
bodyMd:
A fictional public-space team designed benches from replaceable modules. Damaged seats could be changed without discarding the whole bench, and sections could be rearranged for different sites. A prototype was easy to modify in the workshop but awkward to maintain outdoors because its fasteners were difficult to reach after installation.

The team invited maintenance workers to test a revised design using ordinary tools. Their feedback led to fewer fastener types and clearer access points. The designers retained modularity, but stopped treating it as a property guaranteed by a drawing alone. A system could be theoretically separable yet practically troublesome. The value of replacement depended on the work required to carry it out under the conditions in which the bench would actually be used.
